Subject: one small plain pale ivory ceramic bowl of fully cooked Longchuan underground-ant brood soup (陇川蚂蚁蛋汤). A light clear warm broth, with many tiny off-white oval morsels floating naturally and loosely in the liquid, a little natural size variation: most about 1–3 mm with a few about 4–6 mm; these are tiny ingredient grains relative to a roughly 12 cm bowl. Subtle slightly translucent ivory and cream, no dark adult ants, no large eggs, no yolks. Only a few tiny green herb flecks.
Style: gentle realistic watercolor food illustration, clearly hand-painted and illustrative, with soft paper grain and restrained fine detail, never documentary photography. Warm natural white tabletop and warm white background.
Composition: overhead at a slight 25-degree angle, bowl centered and entirely visible; bowl and soup occupy about 70 percent of image width, at least 10 percent clear space on every side. The small ingredient shapes remain legible as food texture without becoming an enlarged insect macro. Soft daylight, calm clean appetizing presentation, no extra props.
Constraints: no lettering, captions, labels, logos, watermarks, people, utensils, fake landmarks, blood, detached parts, adult insects, eggshells, chicken eggs, caviar spheres, caterpillars, legs or wings. Original explanatory illustration only; no claim of species identification or place photography.

Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: original food illustration for a Chinese seasonal ingredient website, square 1:1.
Create an original image from this description, not an edit or copy of any photograph.
Subject: a small serving of five fully cooked intact Chinese oak silkworm pupae, Antheraea pernyi, of the plump pale yellow-brown spring-pupa type associated with Bazhong. On a plain shallow ivory plate, lying flat in a loose natural arrangement with small gaps, each entire pupa visible, no heap. Correct body proportions approximately 3.8 cm long and 1.9 cm at the widest point, stout spindle-shaped with a rounded broad anterior, a smooth fused thoracic case and wing-case seams on the front half, and five to six readable soft transverse abdominal rings tapering gradually to a small blunt posterior. Length only about twice maximum width: not narrow or cylindrical. Light golden tan to soft yellow-brown cooked surfaces, intact, rounded, subtly varied, no black charring. Do not depict caterpillars or white larvae.
Style: gentle realistic watercolor food illustration, visibly hand-painted with soft paper grain, delicate restrained contour detail and calm food-editorial character; not a photographic macro or scientific specimen photo.
Scene: warm natural white tabletop, warm white background, no extra props. Soft natural daylight.
Composition: near-overhead view at a slight angle, the complete shallow plate centered and occupying 70 percent of image width, generous clear background with at least 12 percent margin on all four sides; pupae collectively clearly legible but modest in scale, complete bodies and their real transverse rings visible.
Constraints: no adult insects, no free-standing legs, antennae, wings, eyes, white grubs, cocoons, thin elongated Bombyx mori shapes, blood, openings, detached parts, chopped pieces, exaggerated grotesque macro, text, labels, logos, watermarks, people, utensils, garnish or fake landmarks. Original explanatory illustration only; no claim of species identification or place photography.
